key: I WAS aforetime Manu, I was Surya: I am the sage Kaksivan, holy singer. Kutsa the son of Arjuni I master. I am the sapient Usana behold me.
s: Before the hymn turns to the Falcon who brought the Soma, three verses speak in the first person; Sāyaṇa, on 4.26.1, hears first Vāmadeva, knowing the truth in the womb, speak as the self of all, and bid hearers know their own nature so.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 4.26.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 209120 (2019)

opened.locator: commentary on 4.26.1, and the hymn introduction

evidence.words: इदमादिमन्त्रत्रयेण गर्भे वसन् वामदेवः उत्पन्नतत्त्वज्ञानः सन् सार्वात्म्यं स्वानुभवं मन्वादिरूपेण प्रदर्शयन्नाह । अहं वामदेव इन्द्रो वा मनुरभवं सर्वस्य मन्ता प्रजापतिरस्मि । अहम् एव सूर्यश्च सर्वस्य प्रेरकः सविता चास्मि । विप्रः मेधावी कक्षीवान् दीर्घतमसः पुत्रः एतत्संज्ञकः ऋषिः अप्यहमेव अस्मि । आर्जुनेयम् अर्जुन्याः पुत्रं कुत्सम् एतन्नामकमृषिम् अहम् एव न्यृञ्जे नितरां प्रसाधयामि । "कविः क्रान्तदर्शी "उशना एतदाख्य ऋषिः अहम् एवास्मि । उक्तमुपलक्षणम् । परमार्थदृष्ट्या कृत्स्नमप्यहमेवास्मीत्यर्थः । हे जनाः मा मां सर्वात्मकं पश्यत । यूयमप्येवमेव स्वस्वरूपमनुभवतेत्युक्तं भवति
evidence.gloss: With this and the next two mantras Vāmadeva, dwelling in the womb, knowledge of the real having arisen in him, speaks, showing in the forms of Manu and the rest his own experience of being the self of all. I, Vāmadeva, or Indra, became Manu: I am Prajāpati, the thinker of all. I am also Sūrya, Savitar, impeller of all. The wise Kakṣīvant, son of Dīrghatamas, the sage so named, am I too. Kutsa, son of Arjunī, I greatly further. The far-seeing Uśanas am I. What is said stands for the rest: the meaning is, seen with the eye of the highest truth, I am all of it. O people, see me as the self of all. What is said is: you too, in just this way, experience your own nature.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 4.26.1, at [321,1]). Sāyaṇa on 4.26.1 hears the first three verses as Vāmadeva, in the womb with knowledge of the real arisen (garbhe vasan … utpannatattvajñānaḥ), declaring his being the self of all (sārvātmyam, paramārthadṛṣṭyā kṛtsnam apy aham evāsmi), and closes: see me as the self of all; you too experience your own nature so (yūyam apy evam eva svasvarūpam anubhavata). He also allows Indra as speaker (ahaṃ vāmadevo indro vā; the introduction gives both), which the entry’s ‘first Vāmadeva’ acknowledges; the reading attributed is the one he gives on the verse. Wilson note 1 on 4.26.1 reports the same. Plain sense faithful: 4.26.1 to 3 are first person, 4.26.4 to 7 praise the Falcon who brought the Soma.
